Third deliverable of the data analysis: the main models, the additive
interaction between heatwaves and high ozone, the subgroups and the
attributable mortality burden. The results are preliminary: they use working
definitions that the principal investigator has not confirmed.

::: {.no-download}

| Requested | Where |
|---|---|
| Tables of the individual, joint and interaction models | [Main models and additive interaction](#sec-models) |
| Measures of additive synergy (REOI) | [Additive interaction](#sec-interaction), [by cause of death](#sec-causes) and [across the grid of definitions](#sec-grid) |
| Vulnerability by subgroups | [Vulnerability by subgroups: age and sex](#sec-subgroups) |
| Mortality burden | [Attributable mortality burden](#sec-burden) |
| Initial figures | The figures of each section |
| Commented scripts | [R scripts](#sec-scripts) |

:::

The tables and the figures of this page can be downloaded: each table has an
**Excel** button above it, and each figure a **PNG, 600 dpi** button below it.
Each part names the scripts and the files behind its tables and figures. The
[Methodology](#sec-methodology), which opens the page, describes the data, the
definitions and the methods.

# Methodology {#sec-methodology}

```{r}
#| label: setup-methodology
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "02_plot_style.R"))
library(knitr)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
# Every number quoted in the methodology is computed here, from the
# configuration and the outputs of the scripts
whole <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ",")
method <- list()
method$years <- get_param("study", "years")
method$lags <- unlist(get_param("design", "lags_days"))
method$lag_main <- get_param("models", "lag_main")
method$conf_level <- get_param("models", "conf_level")
method$heatwave_main <- get_param("models", "heatwave_main")
method$ozone_main <- paste0(get_param("air_pollution", "ozone_series_main"), "_",
                            get_param("air_pollution", "interpolation_method_main"))
method$cutoff_main <- get_param("models", "ozone_cutoff_main")
method$cause_groups <- names(get_param("mortality", "cause_groups"))
method$age_labels <- unlist(get_param("mortality", "age_labels"))
method$burden_outcomes <- unlist(get_param("burden", "outcomes"))
method$rate_ages <- unlist(get_param("population", "rate_age_labels"))
method$open_age <- get_param("population", "open_age")
# Step of the continuous ozone term, written in its name (ozone_10ppb)
method$ozone_step <- as.integer(gsub("[^0-9]", "", unique(
  fread(file.path(dir_tables, "models_ozone_continuous.csv"), select = "term")$term)))
method$dataset <- fread(file.path(dir_tables, "case_crossover_summary.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
method$deaths <- method$dataset[grepl("^Deaths \\(strata\\)", item), value]
method$rows <- method$dataset[grepl("^Rows", item), value]
stopifnot(length(method$deaths) == 1, length(method$rows) == 1, length(method$ozone_step) == 1)
# The grid of definitions, as fitted
method_grid <- fread(file.path(dir_tables, "models_grid.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8",
                     select = c("outcome", "heatwave", "ozone", "lag"))
method$grid_heatwaves <- uniqueN(method_grid$heatwave)
method$grid_ozone <- uniqueN(method_grid$ozone)
method$grid_outcomes <- uniqueN(method_grid$outcome)
method$grid_fits <- nrow(method_grid)
stopifnot(method$grid_fits == method$grid_heatwaves * method$grid_ozone *
            method$grid_outcomes * length(method$lags))
rm(method_grid)
```

*Scripts of this deliverable: `Code/30_models_main.R` and
`Code/31_attributable_burden.R`.
[Workflow and scripts](#sec-methods-workflow) lists what each one reads and
writes, and every part of the page names the scripts and the files behind its

## Aim and design {#sec-methods-aim}

The question of the study is whether heatwaves and high ozone, together,
raise mortality more than the sum of their separate effects: an interaction
on the additive scale. This deliverable fits the models that answer it,
measures the interaction, looks at causes of death and at subgroups of age
and sex, and translates the odds ratios into deaths attributable to each
exposure.

The design is a case-crossover study (Maclure, 1991) with referent days
stratified in time and space (Levy and others, 2001; Janes and others, 2005),
built in [deliverable 2](deliverable_2_mortality.html#sec-methodology): each
death is compared with the other days of the same municipality, year, month
and day of the week. The analysis therefore uses only the differences
of exposure between days of the same month in the same place. An odds ratio
of this design estimates the ratio of the daily death rates on exposed and
unexposed days.

The results are preliminary: the definitions of heatwave and of high ozone
are working values that the principal investigator has not confirmed.

| `Data/Derived/exposure_2009_2020.csv` | [Deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-exposure-dataset), `Code/13_exposure_merge_qc.R` | Exposure of every municipality and day, to count the exposed days of the burden |

## Exposure {#sec-methods-exposure}

The definitions are those of
[deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-methodology). For municipality
$m$ and day $t$:

- $HW_{m,t}$ is 1 on a heatwave day and 0 otherwise. Working definition:
  `r method$heatwave_main` (`r heatwave_label(method$heatwave_main)`).
- $O3_{m,t}$ is 1 when ozone is above a percentile of the municipality and 0
  otherwise. Working definition: series `r method$ozone_main` above the
  `r method$cutoff_main`th percentile.
- The compound exposure has four categories: E00 (neither), E10 (heatwave
  only), E01 (high ozone only) and E11 (both).

Each model uses the exposure of one day: the day of death (lag 0) or one of
the `r max(method$lags)` days before it. The lag shown first is lag
`r method$lag_main`, also a working value.

## Models {#sec-methods-models}

*Script: `Code/30_models_main.R`; functions `fit_conditional_logit()`,
`odds_ratios()` and `compound_results()` of `Code/01_functions.R`.*

**Conditional logistic regression.** For death $i$, with referent days $R_i$
(the day of death $d_i$ and its control days) in municipality $m_i$, and
exposure vector $x$ at lag $k$, the contribution to the likelihood is the
probability that, of the days of the stratum, the death falls on the day it
did:

$$L(\beta) = \prod_{i} \frac{\exp\left(x_{m_i,\,d_i-k}^{\top}\,\beta\right)}{\sum_{t \in R_i} \exp\left(x_{m_i,\,t-k}^{\top}\,\beta\right)}.$$

Nothing that is constant within a stratum enters the model: the stratum takes
it out. The coefficients are log odds ratios; intervals are Wald intervals at
`r 100 * method$conf_level`%.

**Four models** for each outcome, subgroup and lag:

| Model | Linear predictor | Reads as |
|:------|:--------|:------------------|
| Heatwave alone | $\beta_1\,HW$ | Odds ratio of death on a heatwave day |
| Ozone alone | $\beta_2\,O3$ | Odds ratio of death on a high-ozone day |
| Joint | $\beta_1\,HW + \beta_2\,O3$ | Each exposure adjusted for the other |
| Compound categories | $\beta_{10}\,E10 + \beta_{01}\,E01 + \beta_{11}\,E11$ | Heatwave only, high ozone only and both, each against neither (E00) |

: Models fitted for each outcome, subgroup and lag. {#tbl-model-forms}

The compound model is the joint model with its interaction written as
categories, and is the one the interaction measures and the burden come from.

**How it is fitted.** Deaths of the same municipality and day share their
referent days and their exposures. The dataset is therefore collapsed to one
row per municipality, day of death and referent day, weighted by the number
of deaths, and fitted with `survival::coxph()` (strata, Breslow method for
ties), which gives the conditional logistic likelihood above. The test suite
shows that the weighted fit equals the fit on the individual records, in
coefficients and in standard errors. A stratum with a missing exposure on any
of its days is left out whole, so that every stratum keeps its day of death.

**Outcomes and subgroups.** The `r length(method$cause_groups)` cause groups
of the plan ([deliverable 2](deliverable_2_mortality.html#sec-methods-causes));
for each, all the deaths, the age groups
`r paste(method$age_labels, collapse = ", ")` and each sex. Two subgroups are
compared with a z-test on the difference of their log odds ratios, which are
estimated on different deaths and are therefore independent.

## Additive interaction {#sec-methods-interaction}

*Function `additive_interaction()` of `Code/01_functions.R`.*

With $OR_{10}$, $OR_{01}$ and $OR_{11}$ the odds ratios of the three exposed
categories of the compound model against E00:

$$\mathrm{REOI} = OR_{11} - OR_{10} - OR_{01} + 1, \qquad
\mathrm{AP} = \frac{\mathrm{REOI}}{OR_{11}}, \qquad
S = \frac{OR_{11} - 1}{(OR_{10} - 1) + (OR_{01} - 1)}.$$

- **REOI**, the relative excess odds due to interaction (the relative excess
  risk due to interaction, with odds ratios in place of risk ratios): the part
  of the excess of the days with both exposures that the two single excesses
  do not add up to. Zero means no additive interaction.
- **AP**, the attributable proportion: that part as a share of $OR_{11}$.
  Zero means no interaction.
- **S**, the synergy index: the excess of the days with both, over the sum of
  the two single excesses. One means no interaction.

Standard errors come from the delta method, with the covariance matrix of the
three log odds ratios (Hosmer and Lemeshow, 1992). The interval of S is built
on the log scale and exists only when the joint excess and the sum of the
single excesses are both positive. The ratio
$OR_{11} / (OR_{10} \times OR_{01})$, the interaction on the multiplicative
scale, is reported next to the three, as recommended for the presentation of
interactions (Knol and VanderWeele, 2012).

## The grid of definitions and continuous ozone {#sec-methods-grid}

- **Grid.** The compound model is fitted for every combination of the
  `r method$grid_heatwaves` heatwave definitions and the
  `r method$grid_ozone` high-ozone flags (three ozone series, two
  interpolation methods, three cut-offs), for `r method$grid_outcomes`
  outcomes and `r length(method$lags)` lags: `r whole(method$grid_fits)` fits.
  It shows how much the answer depends on the definitions. No correction for
  multiple comparisons is applied: without any interaction, about
  `r 100 - 100 * method$conf_level`% of the intervals would still exclude
  zero. The definitions share most of their days, so the cells are not
  independent pieces of evidence.
- **Continuous ozone.** Ozone enters as a linear term, and its odds ratio is
  given per `r method$ozone_step` ppb, for the six ozone series and each lag,
  alone and with the heatwave indicator in the model.

## Attributable mortality burden {#sec-methods-burden}

*Script: `Code/31_attributable_burden.R`; function `attributable_deaths()`
of `Code/01_functions.R`.*

For municipality $i$, calendar year $t$, age group $j$ and exposure category
$c$ (E10, E01 or E11), the analysis plan gives the excess deaths as

$$ED_{itjc} = \text{Population}_{it} \times \text{Age proportion}_{itj} \times \text{Baseline daily rate}_{itj} \times (OR_{jc} - 1) \times \text{Exposure days}_{itc}.$$

The baseline daily rate is the number of deaths per inhabitant and day on the
warm-season days with neither exposure. The first three factors multiply to
the deaths per day on those days, so the population cancels out:

$$ED_{itjc} = \frac{D^{E00}_{itj}}{N^{E00}_{it}} \times (OR_{jc} - 1) \times N^{c}_{it},$$

with $D^{E00}_{itj}$ the deaths on the days with neither exposure and
$N^{E00}_{it}$, $N^{c}_{it}$ the number of days with neither exposure and in
category $c$. This is the form that the script computes.

- **Odds ratios.** Those of the compound model by age group, at the lag set
  in the configuration (lag `r method$lag_main`). Script 31 fits the model
  again to obtain the covariance of the odds ratios, and stops if they differ
  from the table of script 30.
- **Second estimate.** The attributable fraction among the exposed,
  $(OR_{jc} - 1) / OR_{jc}$, applied to the deaths observed on the exposed
  days. It does not assume that the days with neither exposure have the
  baseline mortality of the exposed days, which fall in other weeks of the
  season.
- **Intervals.** By the delta method, from the covariance of the odds ratios.
  Baseline rates and death counts are taken as fixed.
- **Outcomes.** `r sub("^(.)", "\\U\\1", paste(gsub("_", "-", method$burden_outcomes), collapse = " and "), perl = TRUE)`
  mortality.
- **Rates per 100,000.** With the population of the INE projections. The
  projections give single years of age up to `r method$open_age - 1` and one
  group for `r method$open_age` or more, so rates are given for the age groups
  `r paste(method$rate_ages, collapse = " and ")` and for the whole
  population. The excess deaths by the age groups of the plan do not need the
  population.

## Checks {#sec-methods-checks}

The functions behind the models are tested on examples with a known answer
(`tests/test_methods.R`, at the start of every run of `Code/run_all.R`):

| Check | What it shows |
|:----------------|:----------------|
| Weighted fit against the fit on individual records | Same coefficients and standard errors |
| Simulated deaths with known odds ratios | The models recover them |
| REOI, AP and S against `msm::deltamethod` | Same intervals as an independent calculation |
| Attributable deaths | Excess equals expected deaths times OR − 1; categories and groups add up; the delta-method standard error agrees with simulation |

: Checks of the methods of this deliverable. {#tbl-checks}

In the scripts: a fit that gives a warning from the optimiser is counted and
shown, and a category without deaths, where no odds ratio exists, is marked as
not estimable and not as zero.

renders the pages. The scripts are not run when a page is rendered.

| Script | Reads | Writes | Parts of this page |
|:-------|:------|:--------------|:------|
| `Code/30_models_main.R` | `Data/Derived/case_crossover.csv`, `exposure_lagged.csv` | `Output/Tables/models_main_or.csv`, `models_main_interaction.csv`, `models_grid.csv`, `models_ozone_continuous.csv` | Main models and additive interaction; causes; subgroups; grid of definitions; continuous ozone |
| `Code/31_attributable_burden.R` | The same two datasets; `Data/Derived/exposure_2009_2020.csv`; `models_main_or.csv`; INE population projections | `Output/Tables/burden_estimates.csv`, `burden_odds_ratios.csv`, `burden_baseline_rates.csv`, `burden_population.csv` | Attributable mortality burden |
| `tests/test_methods.R` | Nothing: small examples built in the script | The list of checks | Checks |

Shared code: `Code/00_setup.R`, `Code/01_functions.R` (the functions named
above) and `Code/02_plot_style.R`. The fits of script 30 run in parallel; the
results do not depend on the number of processes. All the parameters are in
`config/config.yml`. The code of every script is in [R scripts](#sec-scripts).

## Limits {#sec-methods-limits}

- **Working definitions.** Heatwave, ozone series, cut-off and lag are not
  confirmed; the grid shows how the answer moves with them.
- **One lag per model.** Exposures of consecutive days are correlated, so the
  odds ratio of a lag also carries its neighbours. The models with all the
  lags together are in
  [deliverable 4](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-lag-structure).
- **No adjustment for other pollutants, humidity or temperature here.** It
  is in [deliverable 4](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-sensitivity).
- **Many comparisons.** Causes, subgroups, lags and the grid add up to
  thousands of intervals, none corrected.
- **Exposure of the municipality.** Every resident has the exposure of the
  municipality; the errors of the ozone series are described in
  [deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-ozone-validation).
- **Burden.** The same odds ratio is applied to every municipality and year,
  so differences between them come from baseline mortality and exposed days;
  the intervals carry the uncertainty of the odds ratios only.

# Main models and additive interaction {#sec-models}

*Script: `Code/30_models_main.R`, on the datasets of
`Code/21_case_crossover_dataset.R`. Tables: `Output/Tables/models_main_or.csv`,
`models_main_interaction.csv`, `models_grid.csv` and
`models_ozone_continuous.csv`.*

```{r}
#| label: setup-models
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "02_plot_style.R"))
library(knitr)
theme_set(theme_report())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

read_table <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_tables, file), encoding = "UTF-8")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
ci <- function(estimate, low, high, digits = 2) {
  sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(estimate, digits), fmt(low, digits), fmt(high, digits))
}
# Very wide confidence limits are written as long integers; read them as numbers
as_numeric_columns <- function(dt, pattern) {
  columns <- grep(pattern, names(dt), value = TRUE)
  dt[, (columns) := lapply(.SD, as.numeric), .SDcols = columns]
  dt[]
}
# The synergy index has no useful interval when the sum of the two single
# excesses is close to zero
ci_measure <- function(measure, estimate, low, high, digits = 3) {
  ifelse(measure == "S" & (is.na(low) | high / low > 1e3),
         paste(fmt(estimate, digits), "(interval not informative)"),
         ci(estimate, low, high, digits))
}
main_or <- read_table("models_main_or.csv")
main_int <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("models_main_interaction.csv"), "^(estimate|low|high)$")
grid <- as_numeric_columns(read_table("models_grid.csv"), "^(estimate|low|high|or)_")
continuous <- read_table("models_ozone_continuous.csv")

heatwave_main <- get_param("models", "heatwave_main")
ozone_flag_main <- unique(main_or$ozone)
cause_labels <- c(
  non_accidental = "Non-accidental", cardiopulmonary = "Cardiopulmonary",
  cardiovascular = "Cardiovascular", ischemic_heart = "Ischemic heart disease",
  acute_myocardial_infarction = "Acute myocardial infarction",
  hypertensive = "Hypertensive diseases", cerebrovascular = "Cerebrovascular",
  ischemic_stroke = "Ischemic stroke", hemorrhagic_stroke = "Hemorrhagic stroke",
  respiratory = "Respiratory", copd = "COPD"
)
term_labels <- c(hw = "Heatwave", oz = "High ozone", e10 = "Heatwave only (E10)",
                 e01 = "High ozone only (E01)", e11 = "Heatwave and high ozone (E11)")
model_labels <- c(heatwave = "Heatwave alone", ozone = "Ozone alone", joint = "Joint",
                  compound = "Compound categories")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Preliminary

These results use working definitions that the principal investigator has not
confirmed: heatwave `r heatwave_main`, high ozone `r ozone_flag_main` (the
delivered 24-hour mean, whose limits are shown in the
[validation of the ozone exposure](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-ozone-validation)).
They show that the pipeline runs from the death records to the interaction
measures and how much the answer depends on the definitions. They are not
findings to cite.
:::

## Models

The models are conditional logistic regressions within the strata of the
case-crossover design, one for each single-day lag: each exposure alone, the
two together, and the four compound categories, from which the additive
interaction (REOI, AP, S) is computed. Their forms and formulas are in
[Models](#sec-methods-models) and
[Additive interaction](#sec-methods-interaction).

The days are split at one ozone cut-off, so the reference category (neither)
holds every non-heatwave day at or below it. The plan words the reference as
ozone at or below the 50th percentile; that version, with three ozone levels,
is in the [sensitivity analyses](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-sensitivity).

```{r}
#| label: warnings
n_warn_main <- main_or[!is.na(fit_warnings) & fit_warnings != "", .N]
n_warn_grid <- grid[!is.na(fit_warnings) & fit_warnings != "", .N]
not_estimable <- grid[estimable == FALSE, .N]
```

Fits with a warning from the optimiser: `r n_warn_main` rows of the headline
tables and `r n_warn_grid` cells of the definition grid. Grid cells without
deaths in one exposure category, where no odds ratio exists: `r not_estimable`.

## Non-accidental mortality, working definitions

```{r}
#| label: tbl-main
#| tbl-cap: "Odds ratios (95% confidence interval) for non-accidental mortality by lag."
headline <- main_or[outcome == "non_accidental" & subgroup == "all"]
headline[, `:=`(Model = model_labels[model], Term = term_labels[term],
                value = ci(or, or_low, or_high, 3))]
kable(dcast(headline, factor(Model, levels = model_labels) + factor(Term, levels = term_labels) ~ lag,
            value.var = "value"),
      col.names = c("Model", "Term", "Lag 0", "Lag 1", "Lag 2", "Lag 3"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-main-deaths
#| tbl-cap: "Deaths by exposure category on the lagged day, non-accidental mortality."
counts <- unique(headline[, .(lag, deaths, deaths_e00, deaths_e10, deaths_e01, deaths_e11)])
kable(counts, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Lag", "Deaths", "Neither (E00)", "Heatwave only (E10)",
                    "High ozone only (E01)", "Both (E11)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-main
#| fig-cap: "Odds ratios of non-accidental death by exposure category and lag, compound model. Bars are 95% confidence intervals."
#| fig-height: 3.6
compound <- headline[model == "compound"]
compound[, category := factor(c(e10 = "Heatwave only", e01 = "High ozone only",
                                e11 = "Heatwave and high ozone")[term],
                              levels = c("High ozone only", "Heatwave only", "Heatwave and high ozone"))]
ggplot(compound, aes(factor(lag), or, colour = category)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = ink$axis) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = or_low, ymax = or_high), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
                  linewidth = 0.6, size = 0.35) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_compound[levels(compound$category)]) +
  labs(x = "Lag (days)", y = "Odds ratio", colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: headline-text
h0 <- headline[lag == 0 & model == "compound"]
r_main <- main_int[outcome == "non_accidental" & subgroup == "all" & measure == "REOI"]
```

With the working definitions, on the day of exposure the odds of non-accidental
death are `r ci(h0[term == "e10", or], h0[term == "e10", or_low], h0[term == "e10", or_high])`
times higher on heatwave-only days, `r ci(h0[term == "e01", or], h0[term == "e01", or_low], h0[term == "e01", or_high])`
on high-ozone-only days and `r ci(h0[term == "e11", or], h0[term == "e11", or_low], h0[term == "e11", or_high])`
on days with both, each against days with neither. The associations weaken
with the lag. The joint odds ratio is close to what the two single excesses
add up to: the REOI interval includes zero at every lag
(`r paste(sprintf("lag %d: %s", r_main$lag, ci(r_main$estimate, r_main$low, r_main$high, 3)), collapse = "; ")`).

### Additive interaction {#sec-interaction}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-interaction
#| tbl-cap: "Interaction between heatwave and high ozone, non-accidental and cardiopulmonary mortality. REOI and AP have null value 0; S and the multiplicative ratio have null value 1."
interaction <- main_int[outcome %in% c("non_accidental", "cardiopulmonary") & subgroup == "all"]
interaction[, value := ci_measure(measure, estimate, low, high)]
interaction[, Outcome := cause_labels[outcome]]
kable(dcast(interaction, factor(Outcome, levels = cause_labels[1:2]) +
              factor(measure, levels = c("REOI", "AP", "S", "multiplicative ratio")) ~ lag,
            value.var = "value"),
      col.names = c("Outcome", "Measure", "Lag 0", "Lag 1", "Lag 2", "Lag 3"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-subgroups
#| fig-cap: "Non-accidental mortality by age group and sex: odds ratio of days with both exposures (E11) and REOI, by lag. Bars are 95% confidence intervals."
#| fig-height: 4.6
sub_or <- main_or[outcome == "non_accidental" & subgroup != "all" & model == "compound" & term == "e11",
                  .(subgroup, lag, measure = "Odds ratio, E11", estimate = or,
                    low = or_low, high = or_high, null = 1)]

                     .(subgroup, lag, measure = "REOI", estimate, low, high, null = 0)]
subgroups <- rbind(sub_or, sub_reoi)
subgroups[, subgroup := factor(subgroup, levels = c("0-64", "65-84", "85+", "female", "male"),
                               labels = c("0-64 years", "65-84 years", "85 years or more", "Women", "Men"))]
ggplot(subgroups, aes(factor(lag), estimate)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = null), colour = ink$axis) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), colour = ramp_blue[6], linewidth = 0.5, size = 0.3) +

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-subgroup-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Difference between subgroups in the log odds ratio of the compound exposure (E11): two-sample z-test against the first subgroup of each pair."
e11 <- main_or[outcome == "non_accidental" & model == "compound" & term == "e11" & subgroup != "all",
               .(subgroup, lag, log_or, se)]
pairs <- list(c("0-64", "65-84"), c("0-64", "85+"), c("female", "male"))
tests <- rbindlist(lapply(pairs, function(pair) {
  d <- merge(e11[subgroup == pair[1]], e11[subgroup == pair[2]], by = "lag", suffixes = c("_a", "_b"))
  d[, .(comparison = paste(pair[2], "against", pair[1]), lag,
        ratio_of_odds_ratios = exp(log_or_b - log_or_a),
        z = (log_or_b - log_or_a) / sqrt(se_a^2 + se_b^2))][
    , p_value := 2 * pnorm(-abs(z))]
}))
kable(tests, digits = c(0, 0, 3, 2, 3),
      col.names = c("Comparison", "Lag", "Ratio of odds ratios", "z", "p"))
```

## Across the grid of definitions {#sec-grid}

*Script: `Code/30_models_main.R`. Table: `Output/Tables/models_grid.csv`.*

The compound model was fitted for every combination of the 15 heatwave
definitions, the three ozone series, the two interpolation methods and the
three cut-offs, at each lag. The figure shows the REOI for non-accidental
mortality with the IDW series; a dot marks the cells whose 95% interval
excludes zero. The colour scale stops at ±0.15: the few cells beyond it, all
in the rarest heatwave definitions, are drawn at the limit.

```{r}
#| label: fig-grid
#| fig-cap: "REOI for non-accidental mortality across heatwave definitions (rows) and ozone definitions (columns), by lag, IDW series."
#| fig-height: 13
#| fig-width: 9
g <- grid[outcome == "non_accidental" & grepl("_idw_", ozone) & estimable == TRUE]
g[, series := factor(sub("_idw_gt_p[0-9]+$", "", ozone), levels = c("o3", "o3obs", "o3mda8"),
                     labels = c("Delivered 24 h", "Rebuilt 24 h", "Rebuilt MDA8"))]
g[, cutoff := paste0("> P", sub(".*_gt_p", "", ozone))]
g[, heatwave := factor(heatwave, levels = rev(unique(grid$heatwave)))]
g[, excludes_zero := low_reoi > 0 | high_reoi < 0]
limit <- 0.15
ggplot(g, aes(cutoff, heatwave, fill = estimate_reoi)) +
  geom_tile(colour = ink$surface, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = g[excludes_zero == TRUE], size = 1.2, colour = ink$primary) +
  facet_grid(paste("Lag", lag) ~ series) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = diverging[["low"]], mid = diverging[["mid"]], high = diverging[["high"]],
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-limit, limit), oob = scales::squish, name = "REOI") +
  labs(x = "Ozone cut-off (municipality percentile)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        legend.justification = "center")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grid-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Definition grid, summary by outcome and lag: number of fitted cells, range of the REOI and cells whose 95% interval excludes zero."
grid_summary <- grid[estimable == TRUE, .(
  cells = .N, median_reoi = median(estimate_reoi), min_reoi = min(estimate_reoi),
  max_reoi = max(estimate_reoi), above_zero = sum(low_reoi > 0), below_zero = sum(high_reoi < 0)
), keyby = .(outcome, lag)]
grid_summary[, outcome := cause_labels[outcome]]
kable(grid_summary, digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Outcome", "Lag", "Cells", "Median REOI", "Lowest REOI", "Highest REOI",
                    "Interval above zero", "Interval below zero"))
```

With `r grid[estimable == TRUE, .N]` cells and no correction for multiple
comparisons, about `r round(0.05 * grid[estimable == TRUE, .N])` intervals would
exclude zero by chance alone. The full grid is in `Output/Tables/models_grid.csv`.

### Where the positive cells are

```{r}
#| label: tbl-grid-threshold
#| tbl-cap: "Non-accidental mortality: share of grid cells (%) whose REOI interval lies above zero, by heatwave threshold and lag, with the median REOI."
by_threshold <- grid[estimable == TRUE & outcome == "non_accidental", .(
  cells = .N, above_zero_pct = 100 * mean(low_reoi > 0), median_reoi = median(estimate_reoi)
), by = .(threshold = sub("^hw_(.*)_[0-9]d$", "\\1", heatwave), lag)]
by_threshold[, threshold := factor(threshold, levels = c("p90", "p95", "p99", "30c", "ehf"),
                                   labels = c("> P90", "> P95", "> P99", "> 30 °C", "EHF > 0"))]
kable(dcast(by_threshold, threshold ~ lag, value.var = c("above_zero_pct", "median_reoi")),
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 3),
      col.names = c("Heatwave threshold", paste("% above zero, lag", 0:3), paste("Median REOI, lag", 0:3)))
```

At lags 0 and 1 the grid shows no additive interaction under any definition.
At lags 2 and 3 many intervals lie above zero, and they are concentrated in
the definitions with the fixed 30 °C threshold and the excess heat factor,
while the 95th and 99th percentile definitions show almost none. This is not
yet evidence of synergy. Each model looks at one lag at a time, so the
exposure of two or three days earlier is not separated from the heat of the
days that followed, and days with both exposures belong to longer and hotter
spells than heatwave-only days. The
[analysis of the lag structure](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-lag-structure)
fits the four lags together,
without and with temperature in the model: about half of the positive cells
at lags 2 and 3 remain, and the 30 °C and EHF definitions keep a positive
interaction over the four-day window. That result is exploratory.

# Attributable mortality burden {#sec-burden}

*Script: `Code/31_attributable_burden.R`. Tables:
`Output/Tables/burden_estimates.csv`, `burden_odds_ratios.csv`,
`burden_baseline_rates.csv` and `burden_population.csv`. The map uses
`Data/Derived/municipality_polygons.geojson` (`Code/15_export_geodata.R`).*

```{r}
#| label: setup-burden
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "02_plot_style.R"))
library(knitr)
library(sf)
theme_set(theme_report())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

read_table <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_tables, file), encoding = "UTF-8")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
ci <- function(estimate, low, high, digits = 0) {
  sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(estimate, digits), fmt(low, digits), fmt(high, digits))
}
lag_main <- get_param("models", "lag_main")
heatwave_main <- get_param("models", "heatwave_main")
cutoff_main <- get_param("models", "ozone_cutoff_main")
age_labels <- unlist(get_param("mortality", "age_labels"))
estimates <- read_table("burden_estimates.csv")
odds <- read_table("burden_odds_ratios.csv")
baseline <- read_table("burden_baseline_rates.csv")
population <- read_table("burden_population.csv")

category_names <- c(category_labels, any = "Any of the three")
category_all <- function(x) factor(category_names[x], levels = category_names)
# Headline: non-accidental mortality, working lag, odds ratios by age group
main <- estimates[outcome == "non_accidental" & lag == lag_main & or_source == "age-specific"]
total <- main[level == "total"]
any_total <- total[category == "any"]
pick <- function(category_value, column) total[category == category_value][[column]]
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Preliminary

The burden is computed with the working definitions of the
[main models](#sec-models):
heatwave `r heatwave_label(heatwave_main)`, ozone above the
`r cutoff_main`th percentile of the municipality in the delivered series, and
lag `r lag_main`. The odds ratios are not adjusted for other pollutants; the
[sensitivity analyses](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-sensitivity) show
that adjustment lowers them. The numbers below move with every one of those
choices.
:::

## What is estimated

The formulas are also in
[Attributable mortality burden](#sec-methods-burden) of the methodology.

The number of deaths that would not have occurred on days with a heatwave,
with high ozone or with both, had those days carried the mortality of days
with neither. For each municipality, calendar year and age group the analysis
plan gives

$$
ED = \text{Population} \times \text{Age proportion} \times \text{Baseline daily rate} \times (OR - 1) \times \text{Exposure days}
$$

- **Baseline daily rate**: deaths per inhabitant and day on the warm-season
  days with neither exposure (E00) of that municipality, year and age group.
- **OR**: odds ratio of the exposure category against E00 for that age group,
  from the compound model of the [main models](#sec-models).
- **Exposure days**: warm-season days of that municipality and year in the
  category (heatwave only, high ozone only, both).

The first three factors multiply to the deaths per day on E00 days, so the
population cancels out and the excess is
$(\text{deaths on E00 days} / \text{E00 days}) \times (OR - 1) \times \text{exposure days}$.
The script computes it in that form; the population only enters the rates
per 100,000. The year is the calendar year: the warm-season days of January to
March and of November and December of the same year.

Two things are added to the plan:

- A second estimate, the attributable fraction among the exposed,
  $(OR - 1) / OR$, applied to the deaths observed on the exposed days. It does
  not assume that E00 days and exposed days share the same baseline mortality.
  Heatwaves concentrate in January and February and E00 days are spread over
  the five months, so the two can differ; here they agree (see
  @sec-estimators).
- Confidence intervals by the delta method, from the covariance of the odds
  ratios. Baseline rates and death counts are taken as fixed, and the same
  odds ratio is applied to every municipality and year, so the intervals of
  municipalities and years are not independent of each other.

## Odds ratios and exposed days

```{r}
#| label: tbl-odds
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Odds ratios (95%% confidence interval) used for the burden, non-accidental mortality, lag %d.", lag_main)'
o <- odds[outcome == "non_accidental" & lag == lag_main]
o[, `:=`(group = factor(subgroup, levels = c(age_labels, "all"),
                        labels = c(paste(age_labels, "years"), "All ages")),
         category = category_factor(term),
         value = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f to %.3f)", or, or_low, or_high))]
kable(dcast(o, group ~ category, value.var = "value"), col.names = c("Age group", levels(o$category)))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-days
#| tbl-cap: "Municipality-days of the warm seasons 2009-2020 in each category, deaths observed on them and deaths expected at the baseline rate."
days <- total[, .(category = category_all(category), exposure_days, observed, expected,
                  ratio = observed / expected)]
setorder(days, category)
kable(days, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 3), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Category", "Municipality-days", "Deaths observed", "Deaths expected",
                    "Observed / expected"))
```

The ratio of observed to expected deaths is a crude comparison within
municipality and year. It is close to the odds ratios of the case-crossover
models, which compare within municipality, month and day of the week.

## Excess deaths, 2009-2020

```{r}
#| label: tbl-total
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Excess deaths attributable to each exposure category, warm seasons 2009-2020, lag %d, odds ratios by age group.", lag_main)'
both <- estimates[level == "total" & lag == lag_main & or_source == "age-specific"]
both[, `:=`(cause = factor(cause_labels[outcome], levels = cause_labels[unique(outcome)]),
            category = category_all(category),
            excess_ci = ci(excess, excess_low, excess_high))]
setorder(both, cause, category)
kable(both[, .(cause, category, deaths_total, excess_ci, excess_pct_of_deaths, excess_per_100k)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 2), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Cause", "Category", "Deaths, all days", "Excess deaths (95% CI)",
                    "% of all deaths", "Per 100,000 inhabitants and year"))
```

With the working definitions, `r ci(any_total$excess, any_total$excess_low, any_total$excess_high)`
of the `r fmt(any_total$deaths_total)` non-accidental deaths of the warm
seasons are attributed to heatwaves and high ozone:
`r fmt(pick("e01", "excess"))` to days with high ozone only,
`r fmt(pick("e10", "excess"))` to heatwave days without high ozone and
`r fmt(pick("e11", "excess"))` to days with both. High-ozone days carry the
largest number because they are `r fmt(pick("e01", "exposure_days") / pick("e11", "exposure_days"), 1)`
times as many as the days with both, with a smaller odds ratio.

                   value.var = "exposure_days")

```{r}
#| label: year-2016
frequency <- read_table("compound_frequency_by_year.csv")[heatwave == heatwave_main & year == 2016]
high_share <- function(flag) frequency[ozone == flag, 100 * (e01 + e11) / days]
main_flag <- paste0(get_param("air_pollution", "ozone_series_main"), "_",
                    get_param("air_pollution", "interpolation_method_main"), "_gt_p", cutoff_main)
rebuilt_flag <- sub("^o3_", "o3obs_", main_flag)
```

The years differ through the number of exposed days and the baseline
mortality, not through the odds ratios, which are the same in every year.
Heatwave days are several times more frequent from 2015 on, except in 2018.
In 2016 the delivered ozone series flags `r fmt(high_share(main_flag), 0)`% of
the municipality-days as high ozone, against `r fmt(high_share(rebuilt_flag), 0)`%
in the series rebuilt from the validated hourly records
([validation of the ozone exposure](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-ozone-validation)),
which moves days of that year from "both" to "heatwave only".

::: {.callout-note}
## How to read the map

Every municipality has the same odds ratios, so the map is not a map of
vulnerability to heat or ozone. A municipality has a higher rate when it has
more deaths per inhabitant on ordinary days, which mostly reflects an older
population, or more exposed days. Rates are crude, not standardised by age.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-municipality-year
#| fig-cap: "Excess non-accidental deaths per 100,000 inhabitants by municipality and year, any of the three categories. Municipalities ordered by their rate over the whole period."
#| fig-height: 7.5
my <- main[level == "municipality_year" & category == "any"]
my[, municipality := factor(municipality, levels = rev(by_municipality[order(-excess_per_100k), municipality]))]
ggplot(my, aes(factor(year), municipality, fill = excess_per_100k)) +
  geom_tile(colour = ink$surface, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_magnitude(name = "Per 100,000") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        legend.justification = "center")
```

The table by municipality, year, category and age group is
`Output/Tables/burden_estimates.csv` (`level` is `municipality_year`).

## Baseline mortality and population

```{r}
#| label: tbl-baseline
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Baseline mortality on days with neither exposure, non-accidental deaths, lag %d: deaths per 100,000 inhabitants of the age group and day.", lag_main)'
b <- baseline[outcome == "non_accidental" & lag == lag_main]
# Pooled rate: deaths on E00 days over the person-days at risk on those days
b_summary <- b[, .(deaths = sum(reference_deaths),
                   rate = 1e5 * sum(reference_deaths) / sum(reference_days * population),
                   lowest = min(baseline_daily_rate_per_100k),
                   highest = max(baseline_daily_rate_per_100k)), by = rate_age_group]
kable(b_summary[, .(rate_age_group, deaths, rate, lowest, highest)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 3, 3, 3), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Age group", "Deaths on E00 days", "Rate, all municipalities and years",
                    "Lowest municipality-year", "Highest municipality-year"))
```

The population comes from the INE projections by municipality, sex and single
year of age (base 2017). They give single years up to 79 and one group for 80
years or more, so the age groups 65-84 and 85 or more of the plan have no
population at municipal level. Excess deaths by those age groups are not
affected, because the population cancels out of the formula; rates per 100,000
are given for 0-64 and 65 or more, and for the whole population.
`Output/Tables/burden_baseline_rates.csv` has the baseline rate of every
municipality, year and age group.

## Other lags

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lags
#| tbl-cap: "Excess deaths, any of the three categories, by lag of the exposure (one lag per model)."
lag_table <- estimates[level == "total" & or_source == "age-specific" & category == "any"]
lag_table[, `:=`(cause = factor(cause_labels[outcome], levels = cause_labels[unique(outcome)]),
                 excess_ci = ci(excess, excess_low, excess_high))]
wide <- dcast(lag_table, lag ~ cause, value.var = "excess_ci")
kable(wide, col.names = c("Lag", names(wide)[-1]))
```

Each lag is a separate model, and exposures on consecutive days are
correlated: the rows are not additive across lags. The
[analysis of the lag structure](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-lag-structure)
fits all the lags together.

## Two estimates and two sets of odds ratios {#sec-estimators}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-estimators
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'sprintf("Formula of the plan against the attributable fraction among the exposed, and odds ratios by age group against one odds ratio for all ages. Non-accidental deaths, lag %d.", lag_main)'
compare <- estimates[outcome == "non_accidental" & level == "total" & lag == lag_main]
compare[, `:=`(category = category_all(category),
               plan = ci(excess, excess_low, excess_high),
               fraction = ci(attributable, attributable_low, attributable_high))]
setorder(compare, or_source, category)
kable(compare[, .(or_source, category, plan, fraction)],
      col.names = c("Odds ratios", "Category", "Plan: baseline x (OR - 1) x days",
                    "Observed deaths x (OR - 1) / OR"))
```

```{r}
#| label: estimator-range
ratio <- estimates[level == "municipality_year" & or_source == "age-specific" & lag == lag_main &
                     outcome == "non_accidental" & category == "any", attributable / excess]
```

The two estimates agree in the total and differ by municipality and year,
where the deaths observed on the few exposed days are a small number: the
ratio of the second to the first ranges from `r fmt(min(ratio), 2)` to
`r fmt(max(ratio), 2)` across the `r length(ratio)` municipality-years. One
odds ratio for all ages gives the same total as the odds ratios by age group.

## Limits

- The odds ratios are those of the unadjusted compound model, one lag at a
  time. Adjusting for PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide and humidity lowers them
  ([sensitivity analyses](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-sensitivity)).
- Intervals reflect the uncertainty of the odds ratios only.
- The odds ratio of a category is the same for every municipality and year.
  Differences between municipalities come from baseline mortality and exposed
  days.
- An interval that includes zero in one age group or category does not make
  the excess zero; the estimates are added as they are, negative values
  included.
- The interaction is not significant in the models, so the excess on days with
  both exposures is what the two single excesses add up to, within the
  uncertainty of the data.

# Continued in deliverable 4 {#sec-continued}

- [Sensitivity analyses](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-sensitivity):
  adjustment for PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide, humidity and temperature, three
  ozone levels, alternative ozone series.
- [Lag structure](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-lag-structure): all the
  lags in one model, and the distributed lag non-linear model of temperature.

Not done: the mediation of the heatwave effect by ozone (secondary aim of the
plan), and the choice of the primary lag and of the headline definitions,
which belong to the principal investigator.
